1. What framework this is (Next.js App Router vs Pages Router, React Router, Remix, etc.)
2. How the dashboard-to-project link is implemented today (e.g. <Link href=...>, useRouter().push, etc.) and whether it currently has any prefetch behavior (Next.js Link prefetch prop, React Router loader/lazy, etc.)

Report back: the framework, exact file paths and relevant line numbers/snippets for the dashboard link component, the project page component/loader, and the data fetching calls for title vs. full content. Keep the report focused and under 400 words with concrete file:line references.

<result>This is a small, complete Next.js app — no further route config files exist (checked `next.config.ts`, no `middleware.ts`, no additional route segment files). Report follows.

**Framework:** Next.js App Router (v16 canary), React 19, with `cacheComponents: true` in `/workspace/next.config.ts:4` (the new Cache Components / `"use cache"` model, successor to PPR-style experimental flags).

**1. Dashboard list + links** — `/workspace/app/page.tsx`
- Hardcoded `projects` array (lines 3-6), rendered as a `<ul>` of `<li>` (lines 12-17).
- Link: `app/page.tsx:15` — `<Link href={`/projects/${project.slug}`}>{project.name}</Link>` using `next/link` (import at line 1).
- No explicit `prefetch` prop is set, so it uses Next's default (`prefetch={null}` → auto/viewport prefetch of the route shell in the App Router; with `cacheComponents` on, static shell prefetching applies but there's no per-link tuning here).
- The dashboard already holds `project.name` in memory — this is the "fast" title data, but note it's a separate hardcoded list, not sourced from `lib/data.ts`.

**2. Project page** — `/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`
- Server Component, default export `ProjectPage` (line 4) wraps an inner async `Project` component in `<Suspense fallback={<h1>Loading project...</h1>}>` (lines 5-9).
- `Project` (lines 12-33) awaits `params` (line 15) then runs `Promise.all([getProjectTitle(slug), getProjectDetails(slug)])` (lines 16-19) — both fetched concurrently inside one Suspense boundary, so the fast title data does not resolve/render any earlier than the slow details; there's a single loading fallback for both.

**3. Data fetching** — `/workspace/lib/data.ts`
- `getProjectTitle(slug)` (lines 17-20): marked `'use cache'`, returns instantly from an in-memory `projects` map — the fast path.
- `getProjectDetails(slug)` (lines 22-32): marked `'use cache'`, but has an artificial `await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 800))` (line 24) before returning — the slow/heavy path (description + activity list).
- Both are cached functions (`"use cache"` directive), but there is no differentiated Suspense boundary — since they're combined via `Promise.all` under one `<Suspense>`, the title's fast cache hit is masked by the 800ms details delay. Splitting them into separate Suspense boundaries (or awaiting title outside/before the slow details) would let the title render instantly while details streams in.

**4/5. Route-level prefetch/config:** No route segment config (`export const dynamic`, `revalidate`, `experimental_ppr`) exists in either page file. Only global config is `cacheComponents: true` in `next.config.ts:4`. No loaders (this isn't React Router/Remix), no client-side fetch/useEffect/React Query/SWR anywhere — everything is server-rendered via async Server Components and the `"use cache"` directive.</result>

lastPrompt: When navigating from the dashboard to a project, I want the project's title to appear instantly, but I don't want to prefetch the rest of the project page.

content.text:
This app already uses Next.js Cache Components (PPR-style): a `<Suspense>` boundary marks where the *prefetchable static shell* ends. Right now both the fast title fetch and the slow 800ms details fetch are bundled inside one Suspense with a single fallback, so neither is part of the prefetch — the whole thing waits for the slow fetch after navigation.

The fix is to pull the title out of the Suspense boundary (into the static shell that gets prefetched) and keep only the slow details fetch inside its own Suspense boundary (excluded from prefetch, streamed in after navigation).

content.text:
## Summary

Three changes made this work under the app's `cacheComponents` (Cache Components/PPR) model:

1. **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`** — moved the title fetch out of the page's `<Suspense>` and into the static part of the component; wrapped only the slow details fetch in its own `<Suspense>`.
2. **`lib/data.ts`** — added `generateStaticParams` (via a new `getProjectSlugs()`) so Next can resolve `params` for the known projects at build time, which is required for the title to be included in the prerendered shell at all.
3. **`lib/data.ts`** — removed `'use cache'` from `getProjectDetails`. Without this, Next would bake the (currently static/mock) details data into the build output too, making the *entire* page static and prefetchable — defeating the goal. Removing it keeps details genuinely per-request/dynamic, so they're excluded from what gets prefetched.

Result, confirmed via `next build` and a production server: both `/projects/acme` and `/projects/orbit` now build as Partial Prerenders (◐) — title is instant from the prefetched static shell, while the "Recent activity" details stream in only on actual navigation (full page load measured at ~900ms, matching the simulated fetch delay).

lastPrompt: When navigating from the dashboard to a project, I want the project's title to appear instantly, but I don't want to prefetch the rest of the project page.
